column1: # p250 — `ACTION XK` DISCHARGED. p249 read the 11 education MCP/tutor connectors at Tier A
# only, found 404 on all 16 root paths, and published: "That is the LMS-connector layer of
# this whole industry, and it has no grant ... a studio cannot ship any of them."
# `ACTION XK` asked for Tier B and Tier C before that sentence stands. Both were probed.
# 41 paths per slug: Tier A (16 root licence names) + Tier B (15 non-root) + Tier C (5 manifests).
# ── THE MANIFEST CLAIMS, read first-hand (Tier C is a CLAIM, never a payload: p247 path_class)
# 🔴 0 of 11 reach TIER B. Not one connector hides a licence in docs/, licenses/ or legal/.
#    p249's Tier-A negative was not a reach artefact and the tier ladder adds nothing here.
# 🟢 9 of 11 reach TIER C, and THAT is where p249's conclusion breaks.
# 🔴 6 of the 11 DECLARE `"license": "MIT"` in package.json AND SHIP NO LICENCE TEXT at any
# 🟡 3 reach a manifest that has NO licence field: crevextech/canvas-lms-mcp (package.json),
# 🔴 2 have nothing at all at any of the 41 paths: sujal-shejwal/adaptive-ai-tutor,
# 🔴 "The LMS-connector layer has no grant" is WRONG, and wrong in the direction that costs
#    a studio real options. The accurate statement is TWO statements:
#      • 6 of 11 carry a DECLARED MIT INTENT WITH NO LICENCE TEXT. The npm registry will
#        show MIT for these; the repository ships nothing. That is a known, NAMED and
#        ASKABLE state — an issue asking the author to commit the file they already claim.
#      • 5 of 11 declare nothing anywhere, and those are the ones a studio cannot ship.
# 🔵 This is `p246`/`p247`'s path_class rule doing its job in the useful direction: a
#    manifest field is NOT a grant, so none of the 6 may be published as `MIT` on these
#    shelves — AND recording them as "no grant" erases the one fact that makes them
#    recoverable. The state has a name and it is `DECLARED-NO-PAYLOAD`.
# 🟢 REGION, from a payload rather than from an owner guess: davipac/classroom-mcp's
#    package.json names the package `classroom-aluno-mcp`. "aluno" is Portuguese for
#    student. 🟡 It places the package's LANGUAGE, not the author's country — recorded as a
#    language signal consistent with LATAM, not as an evidenced LATAM row.
